diff --git a/test/units/module_utils/facts/test_sysctl.py b/test/units/module_utils/facts/test_sysctl.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..f97c5c0
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/units/module_utils/facts/test_sysctl.py
@@ -0,0 +1,92 @@
+from __future__ import (absolute_import, division, print_function)
+__metaclass__ = type
+
+import errno
+
+import pytest
+
+from units.compat.mock import Mock, patch
+
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.sysctl import get_sysctl, get_uptime_facts
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.hardware.freebsd import FreeBSDHardware
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.hardware.netbsd import NetBSDHardware
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.hardware.openbsd import OpenBSDHardware
+
+
+def module_with_sysctl(result):
+    module = Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.return_value = result
+    return module
+
+
+def test_sysctl_parses_formats_and_continuations():
+    module = module_with_sysctl((0, 'hw.ncpu=4\nkern.osrelease: 7.5\n'
+                                 'kernel.hostname host\nkern.notes: first\n'
+                                 '  second\n\n  fourth\n', ''))
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw', 'kern']) == {
+        'hw.ncpu': '4', 'kern.osrelease': '7.5',
+        'kernel.hostname': 'host', 'kern.notes': 'first\n  second\n\n  fourth'}
+    module.warn.assert_not_called()
+
+
+def test_sysctl_warns_and_keeps_valid_lines():
+    module = module_with_sysctl((0, 'badline\nhw.ncpu: 2\nalso_bad\nkern.boottime=123\n', ''))
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw', 'kern']) == {'hw.ncpu': '2', 'kern.boottime': '123'}
+    assert module.warn.call_count == 2
+    assert module.warn.call_args_list[0][0][0].startswith('Unable to split sysctl line (badline): ')
+    assert module.warn.call_args_list[1][0][0].startswith('Unable to split sysctl line (also_bad): ')
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('failure', [(1, '', 'permission denied'), OSError('broken pipe'), IOError('read failed')])
+def test_sysctl_command_failure(failure):
+    module = module_with_sysctl(failure if isinstance(failure, tuple) else (0, '', ''))
+    if not isinstance(failure, tuple):
+        module.run_command.side_effect = failure
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw']) == {}
+    assert module.warn.call_args[0][0].startswith('Unable to read sysctl: ')
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('hardware', [FreeBSDHardware, NetBSDHardware, OpenBSDHardware])
+def test_bsd_uptime(hardware):
+    module = module_with_sysctl((0, '100\n', ''))
+    with patch('ansible.module_utils.facts.sysctl.time.time', return_value=150):
+        assert hardware(module).get_uptime_facts() == {'uptime_seconds': 50}
+    module.run_command.assert_called_once_with(['/sbin/sysctl', '-n', 'kern.boottime'])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('result', [(1, '100', 'failed'), (0, '', ''), (0, 'n/a', ''),
+                                    (0, '{ sec = 100 }', '')])
+def test_uptime_omitted_for_failed_or_non_numeric_output(result):
+    module = module_with_sysctl(result)
+    assert get_uptime_facts(module) == {}
+
+
+def test_uptime_missing_binary_raises_value_error():
+    module = module_with_sysctl((0, '100', ''))
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = None
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_uptime_facts(module)
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.side_effect = OSError(errno.ENOENT, 'No such file or directory')
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_uptime_facts(module)
+    module.run_command.side_effect = None
+    module.get_bin_path.side_effect = OSError(errno.ENOENT, 'No such file or directory')
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_uptime_facts(module)
+
+
+def test_openbsd_populate_combines_all_fact_sources():
+    hardware = OpenBSDHardware(module_with_sysctl((0, '', '')))
+    sources = ('get_processor_facts', 'get_memory_facts', 'get_device_facts',
+               'get_dmi_facts', 'get_mount_facts', 'get_uptime_facts')
+    expected = {}
+    for name in sources:
+        fact = name.replace('get_', '').replace('_facts', '')
+        setattr(hardware, name, Mock(return_value={fact: name}))
+        expected[fact] = name
+    with patch('ansible.module_utils.facts.hardware.openbsd.get_sysctl', return_value={}):
+        assert hardware.populate() == expected
+    for name in sources:
+        getattr(hardware, name).assert_called_once_with()
